Enterprise Data Program Delivery

Lead complex, multi-year data and analytics initiatives with accountability for end-to-end delivery, business outcomes, and executive visibility.
Drive delivery across enterprise data platform modernization, shared data services, data products, data governance, metadata management, data quality, data integration, migration, reporting and analytics enablement, and AI/ML foundations.
Develop and manage integrated program plans, roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, decisions, readiness criteria, adoption measures, and delivery risks.
Ensure delivery aligns with enterprise data strategy, architecture direction, business priorities, and committed outcomes.

Partner directly with Data Engineering, Architecture, Analytics, Product, Security, and application teams to understand technical concepts, design decisions, delivery models, dependencies, and operational impacts.
Validate delivery sequencing, implementation readiness, migration plans, integration approaches, and downstream consumer impacts.
Engage credibly in discussions involving source ingestion, ETL/ELT pipelines, cloud data platforms, data warehouses and lakehouses, APIs and integrations, data lineage, metadata, data quality, reporting ecosystems, and AI/ML enablement.
Translate technical discussions into actionable plans, clear ownership, decisions, and executive-ready communications.

Own scope, schedule, financials, resources, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, change control, delivery health, and governance for assigned programs.

Manage dependencies involving source-system readiness, ingestion, platform capabilities, environment availability, migration sequencing, downstream reporting, analytics and AI consumers, and operational support.
Lead cross-team working sessions to resolve blockers, align priorities, clarify decisions, and maintain delivery momentum.
Serve as an accountable program leadership point across teams and partners, maintaining continuity even as delivery models or resources change.

Own program-level budget planning, forecasting, variance management, and investment transparency for assigned programs.
Lead cross-initiative capacity and resource planning for transformational data programs, partnering with Data and Technology leaders to identify constraints, trade-offs, and sequencing impacts. Functional leaders retain accountability for managing their team capacity.
Manage implementation and delivery partners as strategic contributors, holding them accountable for outcomes, integration quality, committed deliverables, and alignment with enterprise architecture and operating models.
Partner with platform product owners as they manage software and platform vendor relationships, contracts, and service expectations.

Description

Senior Supply Chain Program Manager - Hybrid

The Senior Program Manager provides strategic guidance to service segment or functional teams in a way that advances the Mission and Core Values of Providence St. Joseph Health. The position leads category management activities, including category strategy development, spend and market analysis, stakeholder engagement, supplier relationship and performance management, and the identification and execution of sourcing and value-improvement opportunities. The Senior Program Manager also oversees the assessment, development, deployment, and adoption of programs and initiatives that improve Experience, Delivery, Quality, and Cost. In partnership with PSJH leaders, clinical and operational stakeholders, and suppliers, the Senior Program Manager develops and implements efficient strategies and tactics that address systemic and acute issues, strengthen category performance, and deliver sustainable enterprise value.

Providence caregivers are not simply valued – they’re invaluable. Join our team at Supply Chain Management and thrive in our culture of patient-focused, whole-person care built on understanding, commitment, and mutual respect. Your voice matters here, because we know that to inspire and retain the best people, we must empower them.

jobs.title: Business analyst
jobs.description:
At Bending Spoons, we’re striving to build one of the all-time great companies. A company that serves a huge number of customers. A company where team members grow to their full potential. A company that functions at unparalleled levels of effectiveness and efficiency. A company that creates value for shareowners at an extraordinary rate. And a company that does so while adhering to high ethical standards.

In pursuit of this objective, we acquire and improve digital businesses, not to sell on, but to own and operate for the long term. The transformations we make are often deep—designed to speed up innovation, benefit customers, and strengthen business performance. Here, hierarchy is minimal and teams are small and talent-dense. We operate established products with the ambition, agility, and urgency of a startup. Across the company, we integrate AI deeply into how we work so that human judgment and machine intelligence reinforce each other.

For a talented, driven, and collaborative individual, working at Bending Spoons is an opportunity to learn, make an impact, and progress their career at an exceptionally high rate. That’s our promise to such a candidate.

A few examples of your responsibilities
Understand.
Build a 360° understanding of your product, users, business model, competitive landscape, and economics. Use AI, data, and research to uncover key business drivers, diagnose challenges, and identify opportunities for growth and product development.
Ideate.
Turn insights into concrete opportunities and hypotheses for testing. Explore new products features, growth initiatives, monetization opportunities, and improvements to how the business operates, prioritizing those with the greatest potential impact.
Execute.
Turn the most promising opportunities into action and clear customer value. Support roadmap conversations with enterprise clients, build the business case, and work cross-functionally with engineering, design, and other teams to bring initiatives to life.
Optimize.
Use A/B tests, business and product metrics, and ongoing analysis to understand what works and what doesn’t. Scale successful initiatives, improve existing ones, and use each result to inform the next cycle of discovery and execution.

What we look for
Reasoning ability.
Given the necessary knowledge, you can solve complex problems. You think from first principles, and structure your ideas sharply. You resist the influence of biases. You identify and take care of the details that matter.
Drive.
You’re extremely ambitious in everything you do—and your initiative, effort, and tenacity match the intensity of your ambition. You feel deeply responsible for your work. You hold yourself to a high—and rising—bar.
Team spirit.
You give generously and without the expectation of receiving in return. You support the best idea, not your idea. You're always happy to get your hands dirty to help your team. You’re reliable, honest, and transparent.
Proficiency in English.
You read, write, and speak proficiently in English.

What we offer
Incredibly talented, entrepreneurial teams.
You’ll work in small, result-oriented, autonomous teams alongside some of the brightest people in your field.
An exceptional opportunity for growth.
We go to great lengths to hire individuals of outstanding potential—then, our priority is to put them in the ideal position to thrive. Spooners in their 20s lead products worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And if you’ve got what it takes, you’ll soon be playing an essential role in major projects, too.
All. These. Benefits.
Flexible hours, remote working, unlimited backing for learning and training, top-of-the-market health insurance, a rich relocation package, generous parental support, and a yearly retreat to a stunning location. We help each Spooner set up the conditions to do their best work.
Competitive pay and access to company equity at a discount.
Typical annual salary offers range from £85,797 to £151,436 in London and from €66,065 to €107,837 elsewhere in Europe. The lower end of these ranges applies to candidates with little or no relevant experience, while exceptionally experienced candidates may receive offers of up to £316,052 in London or €240,330 elsewhere in Europe. Candidates offered a permanent contract may choose to receive part of their compensation in discounted company equity.

Commitment & contract

Permanent or fixed-term. Full-time or part-time.

Location

Milan (Italy), London (UK), Madrid (Spain), Warsaw (Poland), or fully remote from eligible countries.

The selection process

In our screening process, we prioritize verifiable signals of excellence, regardless of seniority. There are no preferential paths beyond what your application demonstrates, and we evaluate every candidate through the same process.

Some people hold back because they feel they lack experience or have an “imperfect” CV. If you like the role and believe you could excel over time, don’t self-reject.

All applications go through our careers page, which is the only way to be considered. If you pass our screening, you’ll be asked to complete one or more tests. They are challenging, may involve unfamiliar problems, and can take several hours. To learn more about what to expect throughout the selection process, you can find additional information here.

We set the bar high and won’t extend an offer until we’re confident we’ve found the right candidate. This is why a job may remain open for months or be reposted several times.

We consider all applicants for employment and provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities—please let us know through this form.

Before you apply

If you’ve applied before but didn't receive an offer, we recommend waiting at least one year before applying again.

Bending Spoons is a demanding environment. We’re extremely ambitious and we hold ourselves—and one another—to a high standard. While this tends to lead to extraordinary learning, achievement, and career growth, it also requires significant commitment.

To help you ramp up quickly and set yourself up for success, we expect you to spend most days in our Milan office during your first few months with us, regardless of your long-term work location. It’s the best way to rapidly absorb our company culture and build trust with your new teammates. We’ll support you with generous travel and accommodation assistance. After that, you’re welcome to work from one of our offices, or remotely from approved countries—depending on what we agree at the offer stage.

If the role speaks to you and you’re excited to give your best, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now—we can’t wait to meet you.

Turn complex implementations into successful customer outcomes

We’re looking for a Technical Program Manager
who thrives in a global environment and enjoys operating at the intersection of customer success, engineering, product, and delivery
.

This isn’t a role where you simply track timelines or coordinate meetings.

You’re the person who turns complexity into a clear, executable plan and delivers it.

You’ll own the successful implementation of Bidgely’s platform for utilities across the US,
Europe and the Middle East

If you enjoy turning complex technical deployments into real-world outcomes for customers, this role will feel energizing.

Why This Role Exists

Utilities around the world are rapidly modernizing their infrastructure as EV adoption, distributed solar, batteries, and smart devices reshape the grid.

Bidgely helps utilities navigate that transformation through AI-powered energy insights and customer engagement platforms
.

As demand for our platform grows internationally, we need experienced Technical Program Managers who can confidently guide utilities through complex implementations, aligning stakeholders, solving technical challenges, and ensuring customers see real value from the platform.

Your mission over the next 6-12 months
is simple:

Deliver successful customer implementations that turn powerful technology into measurable outcomes for utilities.

How You’ll Make an Impact

You’ll own the delivery and technical implementation
of Bidgely’s platform for enterprise utility customers.

In practice, that means you will:

Lead customer implementations end-to-end

Own enterprise deployments from onboarding through launch, ensuring projects stay on track and deliver measurable customer value.

You’re confidently managing customer implementations, running project meetings, and collaborating with engineering teams on integration planning.

You understand Bidgely’s platform architecture and can clearly translate customer requirements into implementation plans.

At 12 months

You’ve successfully delivered multiple enterprise deployments.

Customers view you as a trusted advisor who can navigate technical complexity and keep projects moving.

Your work directly contributes to successful launches, satisfied customers, and expansion opportunities.

What Makes Someone Successful Here

Ownership.

The strongest TPMs here don’t just manage timelines. They own outcomes
.

They ask questions early, surface risks quickly, and collaborate across teams to keep complex implementations moving forward.

Strong Technical Program Managers at Bidgely:

Connect technical details to business outcomes
Stay calm when implementations get messy
Ask the right questions before proposing solutions
Communicate clearly with both engineers and executives
Take pride in delivering high-quality customer experiences

Manage project timelines, risks, dependencies, and deliverables

Work directly with customer engineering teams on data integrations, APIs, and system architecture
Translate customer requirements into scalable technical solutions
Guide requirement analysis, integration planning, and implementation execution
Identify product gaps and collaborate with Product teams on enhancements

Customer Success & Market Impact

Develop deep expertise in the utility and energy markets
Ensure customers achieve measurable value from the platform
Identify opportunities for future growth within customer accounts
Occasionally travel to Bidgely headquarters in Los Altos, CA

What You’ll Bring

Required Qualifications

5–7 years managing software implementation or integration programs at a technology company
Experience delivering complex enterprise implementations for high-touch customers
Proven experience serving as the primary point of contact for enterprise customers
Experience collaborating with globally distributed teams and offshore engineering resources
Strong experience designing and delivering cloud-based B2B implementations
Ability to manage project plans, risks, and deliverables using tools such as Jira, Smartsheets, or similar platforms
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Customer-first mindset and strong relationship-building skills

Experience implementing SaaS platforms for enterprise customers

jobs.description:
Description

Amazon’s Bug Bounty team is looking for a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to help us secure the services and applications that Amazon customers rely on every day. In this role, you’ll drive complex, cross-functional programs that improve how we identify, triage, and resolve externally reported security vulnerabilities. You’ll work across engineering, security, and business teams to improve processes, remove roadblocks, and ensure researchers have the access and support they need to help raise our security bar.

You’ll partner with internal teams to close vulnerabilities quickly and effectively, and you’ll help shape the future of how Amazon engages with the global security research community. This is a fast-paced, high-impact role that requires strong ownership, sound judgment, and the ability to dive deep into technical problems while keeping stakeholders aligned.

Key job responsibilities

Lead technical programs that improve how Amazon responds to externally reported vulnerabilities
Define and scale internal processes for vulnerability intake, triage, and resolution
Build durable solutions that reduce repeat issues through automation, better tooling, and improved service team accountability
Collaborate with partner teams to improve test account support and ensure researchers have the access they need to test securely and effectively
Communicate clearly and regularly with senior leaders, engineering teams, and external researchers
Own the long-term roadmap for specific areas of the Bug Bounty program and influence the broader team strategy

A day in the life

You will spend most days working with engineers, builder teams, and partner teams to improve how we handle bug bounty findings. You might be mapping out a plan to improve processes, coordinating across teams to roll out new tools, or identifying where we need better support for internal owners. Some days will focus on clearing blockers and aligning stakeholders. Others will focus on building the right systems to scale the program as Amazon grows.

About The Team

The Bug Bounty team helps protect Amazon and its customers by working with external security researchers who report vulnerabilities in our public-facing services. We partner with security engineers and builder teams across the company to investigate findings, improve our response processes, and build systems that scale. Our mission is to raise the security bar across Amazon by learning from every bug. We value clear thinking, sound judgment, and strong ownership, and we work every day to make Amazon more secure for customers around the world.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture

In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

3+ years of technical product or program management experience
2+ years of software development experience
3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

Success in this role requires agility in communication, with the ability to engage confidently with executives while working closely with technical teams and individual contributors.

The Technology Vendor Manager plays a critical role in aligning vendor strategy with the organization’s technology and business objectives. This position works across operations, enterprise architecture, sourcing, and IT leadership to manage vendor and support program reporting to executives to enable strategic decision-making. The role ensures technology purchases are optimized, integrated, and aligned with the company’s multi-year capital and expense investment plans.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
JOB TITLE:
Project Manager
LOCATION:
Remote - must be willing to work across timezones
DURATION:
6 months
RATE RANGE:
$60-$70/hr
POSITION SUMMARY:

Lead business and functional projects from definition through handoff, creating clarity across stakeholders, plans, decisions, risks, dependencies, and outcomes. This role is designed for an experienced business-oriented Project Manager who can quickly establish governance, translate business objectives into executable plans, and drive cross-functional delivery. Technical fluency is valuable, but deep technical project management is not the primary focus.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Project definition and planning. Partner with sponsors and business leaders to clarify objectives, scope, success measures, deliverables, assumptions, constraints, resources, milestones, and decision rights.
• Delivery leadership. Build and maintain integrated project plans; coordinate work across functional teams; monitor progress; and drive timely execution through completion and operational handoff.
• Stakeholder alignment. Establish productive relationships with sponsors, functional leaders, subject matter experts, vendors, and other partners. Facilitate clear decisions, commitments, and accountability.
• Governance and reporting. Create an appropriate operating rhythm, including status reporting, working sessions, steering updates, decision logs, and action tracking. Escalate clearly and at the right time.
• Risk and dependency management. Identify, assess, document, and actively manage risks, issues, assumptions, constraints, and cross-project dependencies.
• Change control. Evaluate proposed changes to scope, schedule, cost, resources, and expected outcomes; document impacts and guide stakeholders through approval and prioritization decisions.
• Business process focus. Map current and future-state processes, surface gaps, coordinate requirements, and support practical improvements that are sustainable after project close.
• Adoption and transition. Coordinate readiness, communications, training, documentation, stakeholder feedback, and handoff activities with the accountable business owners.
• Continuous improvement. Capture lessons learned and recommend fit-for-purpose improvements to project practices, workflows, templates, and governance.

Expected Deliverables

• Approved project charter or equivalent project definition, including scope, outcomes, governance, and success measures.
• Integrated project plan with milestones, owners, dependencies, and critical decisions.
• Current status reporting and maintained logs for risks, issues, actions, decisions, and changes.
• Stakeholder and governance cadence with documented outcomes and follow-up.
• Business requirements and process documentation at the level appropriate to the engagement.
• Readiness, transition, and handoff materials that support ownership after the engagement.
• Project closeout summary, including outcomes, open items, and lessons learned.

Engagement Principles

• Outcome-oriented. The contractor is engaged to deliver defined project outcomes and artifacts, with priorities and milestones agreed with the designated sponsor.
• Collaborative. The role works across internal teams and may coordinate third parties, while respecting established decision rights and accountable business ownership.
• Adaptable. The contractor should apply an appropriate level of project rigor based on risk, complexity, pace, and stakeholder needs.
• Confidential and compliant. The contractor must follow applicable confidentiality, information security, data handling, access, and conduct requirements communicated for the engagement.

Measures of Success

• Clear, shared understanding of scope, outcomes, ownership, milestones, and decision paths.
• Timely visibility into project health, risks, decisions, dependencies, and required leadership actions.
• Deliverables meet agreed acceptance criteria and are transitioned to accountable business owners.
• Stakeholders are aligned, informed, and able to make decisions with the information provided.
• Project documentation is current, usable, and proportionate to project complexity

QUALIFICATIONS:

• Demonstrated experience independently leading complex business or functional projects with cross-functional stakeholders.
• Strong command of project management fundamentals, including planning, governance, scope, schedule, cost awareness, risks, issues, dependencies, change control, and status reporting.
• Ability to translate broad business objectives into clear workstreams, deliverables, ownership, and measurable outcomes.
• Executive-ready written and verbal communication, with the judgment to tailor detail for sponsors, leaders, and project teams.
• Proven facilitation, negotiation, and influence skills in matrixed environments where authority may be indirect.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to synthesize incomplete or conflicting information and drive decisions.
• Experience with business process analysis, operational improvement, organizational change, or business transformation initiatives.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities, work with limited direction, and bring structure to ambiguous situations.
• Proficiency with standard project planning, collaboration, reporting, presentation, and documentation tools.
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

Preferred Qualifications

• Project management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, or an equivalent credential.
• Experience supporting globally distributed teams or multi-region initiatives.
• Experience working within a formal PMO, portfolio governance model, or strategic planning environment.
• Technical aptitude sufficient to partner effectively with IT, data, systems, security, and vendor teams when a business project has technical dependencies.
• Working knowledge of portfolio or strategic portfolio management tools.
• Experience with process mapping, requirements elicitation, change management, or operational readiness.

BENEFITS SUMMARY:
Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Compensation details listed in this posting reflect the base hourly rate or annual salary only, unless otherwise stated. In addition to base compensation, full-time roles are eligible for Medical, Dental, Vision, Commuter and 401K benefits with company matching.

jobs.description:
Prolific Machines is ushering in a new era of biotechnology with light. Our first-of-its-kind optogenetic platform delivers unprecedented control, precisely guiding cellular behavior when and where it matters most. Unlike existing tools used to control biology, our technology enables dynamic, tunable control over virtually any cellular function in any cell type. We're enabling partners to unlock robust efficiency, quality, and reproducibility advantages across the most complex pharmaceuticals and therapeutic proteins. Prolific is supported by leading investors, including Bill Gates’s Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Mayfield and SOSV.

We’re looking for a Technical Project Manager with experience in leadership/management of innovative scientific projects to manage critical customer programs in Prolific’s pipeline. As Prolific has developed a unique form of cellular control using optogenetics, these projects can include, but are not limited to:

R&D efforts focused on building new capabilities.
Enabling pharmaceutical partners to build optogenetic capabilities at their sites.
Full cell line development and preclinical scale up of customer molecules integrated into our optogenetic cell lines.

Technical project scoping, planning, and schedule oversight of internal and client-facing projects
Resource planning with senior leadership to forecast project needs, scope alignment, and schedule coordination

Research & Development, cell line development, process development, analytics, hardware, business development and product development teams for cross-functional coordination to make key decisions on tech transfers and technical support
Client/ customer teams including technical leads, business development representatives, and senior leadership
Third-parties, suppliers and partners for necessary capital equipment to support our teams

You have good verbal and written communication skills with a focus on clarity and conciseness in a team-oriented environment
You are willing to bring your technical acumen to help with team challenges and addressing technical obstacles

Job Description

POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Operations Project Manager I is responsible for ensuring on-time and on-budget delivery of high-quality products by coordinating and managing the activities of Manufacturing, Engineering, Project Management and Purchasing as well as verifying that all needed information such as drawings, specifications, bills of material (BOM), work orders, and materials are available and accurate prior to and during the manufacturing process. Additional responsibilities include shop-floor scheduling and control, work order creation/maintenance, production resource management, and Operations process improvement. Coordinate outside venders and sub-contractors as required.

Key Job Responsibilities

Develop Production / Project Execution Plan for the assigned project to meet delivery schedule.
Review and verify drawings, specifications, BOMs, work orders and material availability prior to and during manufacturing.
Participate in labor forecast planning & developing manufacturing strategy for the projects.
Ensure balanced or level shop workload.
Track and report progress to the manufacturing and project schedules & monitor in-process work orders and communicate progress.
Participation as a key-member of the project team, along with the PM and PE.
Work closely with the EPC Scheduler on internal, customer and vendor schedules to ensure that execution plans are in alignment.
Coordinate work and communication between Manufacturing, Engineering, Project Management, Purchasing, Quality, Logistics and Production Planning.
Perform in-house expediting as needed to maintain schedule deliverables.
Requisition of project materials, as needed.
Coordination and documentation of TAS rework occurrences. Monitor and report root causes as well as financial or schedule impacts resulting from non-conformances.
Facilitation of the revision control/”red line” process.
Participation and coordination of project team meetings.
Any other responsibilities as assigned by TAS.

Job Skills

Familiarity with project performance metrics such as Earned Value Analysis (EVA), Cost Performance Index and Schedule Performance Index.
Committed to excellence and high standards; must be willing to foster a positive environment.
Strong organizational, problem solving and analytical skills.
Ability to work multiple projects simultaneously and function in a fast-paced environment.
A self-starter that can manage multiple priorities with minimal supervision.
Ability to communicate effectively and professionally with superiors and peers as well as with individuals both inside and outside the company.
Proficient in MS Excel, Word, Outlook & knowledge of Primavera / MS Project usage.

Education & Training

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial or Mechanical Engineering from an accredited four-year engineering program.
A substitution of military leadership and/or technical work experience will be considered in lieu of an engineering degree
Six Sigma Green Belt Certification would be a plus

Minimum Requirements

3-5 years of experience as an Industrial/Manufacturing Engineer, Operations Manager, other related role in a heavy/industrial manufacturing environment.
Familiarity with Fabrication, Welding & Assembly processes.
Experience in developing & monitoring Labor Budgets, ETC / EAC for the projects.
Proficiency in ERP system is required.
Experience in building and working with bills of material and monitoring work orders in an MRP system.
High proficiency in Blue Print reading and P&ID interpretation.
Experience with Lean (or other waste elimination processes), ISO 9001 (or other QMS).

Preferred Requirements

Ability to exert up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Performs other physical activities including use of fingers, stooping, crouching, talking, hearing and performing repetitive motions. Visual acuity requirements include color, depth perception and field of vision necessary to prepare and analyze data and figures, operate a computer terminal and conduct extensive reading. The incumbent will be subject to inside environmental conditions. The ability to work overtime and some weekends will be required.

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

Position is at least 80% to 95% at a desk working with computer. Ability to exert up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Performs other physical activities including use of fingers, sitting, stooping, bending, crouching, talking, hearing, and performing repetitive motions. Visual acuity requirements include color, depth perception and field of vision necessary to prepare and analyze data and figures, operate a computer terminal, and conduct extensive reading. The incumbent will be subject to inside environmental conditions.

Company Overview

Join a team driven to excel in all that we do! When you join TAS, you join a Houston-headquartered company that is part of a large Houston-headquartered publicly traded company, Comfort Systems USA, with a solid reputation built on outstanding value, integrity, and customer focus. We offer our customers and employees the best of both worlds: a small company feel with the resources, talent, process, and international reach of a large company.

TAS delivers innovative packaged modular systems that are engineered and manufactured in one of our Houston, TX facilities and utilized in data centers, power, and commercial/industrial utility system applications. TAS has successfully delivered and commissioned over 520 packages to over 33 countries. The company is headquartered in Houston, TX and has five ISO 9001 certified manufacturing facilities in Houston, encompassing 1.2m sq. feet with proximity to major shipping ports and interstate highways. TAS manages all logistics and transportation facilitating accelerated construction at customer’s facilities.

TAS’ fastest growing business is the data center market. By applying deep expertise in cooling, thermodynamics, and power, TAS has developed an entire product line that revolutionizes data center delivery.

The Program Manager, Workday HR Technology
will play a pivotal role in transforming how Essex leverages technology to support its people and business. Partnering closely with HR, IT, Finance, Operations, and executive stakeholders, you'll spearhead innovative HR technology solutions that enable a dynamic, geographically distributed workforce while influencing the future of HR systems at Essex.

What You Will Do

Lead end-to-end Workday implementation and enhancement projects across HCM, Payroll, Learning, Talent, Recruiting, Compensation and Time & Absence modules, tailored to support corporate, and operations staff.
Serve as primary liaison between HR, Payroll, Finance, Operations, and IT stakeholders, plus third-party implementation partners.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts in a clear and concise manner.
A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset with attention to detail.
Ability to build strong partnerships with HR, Payroll, IT, and business stakeholders.
Drive for continuous improvement and innovation in HR systems and processes.

Ability to work Monday through Friday. Role may be hybrid or remote based on proximity to an Essex corporate office; candidates must reside in California or Washington. Work involves extended periods at a desk using standard office equipment (e.g., computer, phone, printer), with minimal physical exertion.
Occasional travel may be required for meetings, training, or conferences.

Ability to manage multiple, time sensitive HR system projects throughout the year, based on current priorities.
A strategic mindset to leverage HR Technology to meet the needs/requirements of our corporate and property management operations.
Effective and proactive communication to drive trust and conﬁdence within HR technology.

Certification: SnowPro Core or SnowPro Advanced Certified.
Platform Experience: Direct hands-on experience with the Snowflake AI Data Cloud, including proficiency in SQL and/or Python.
Assessment Tools & Standards: Experience with item banking platforms (e.g., Pearson ExamDeveloper) and assessment standards like QTI (Question & Test Interoperability).

jobs.title: Senior Competitive & Market Intelligence Manager
jobs.description:
WEKA is the AI data and memory infrastructure company transforming how organizations build, run, and scale AI. NeuralMesh™ combines high-performance data storage and extended GPU memory in a single software platform, providing a foundation for training, inference, and agentic AI workloads that maximizes GPU productivity, accelerates AI outcomes, and improves the economics of AI at scale.

WEKA is a pre-IPO, growth-stage company backed by world-class venture capital investors and AI infrastructure leaders. Our technology is trusted by 30% of the Fortune 50, as well as leading hyperscalers, neoclouds, AI builders, and research organizations. Our team is customer-obsessed, accountable, bold, and collaborative, with a shared focus on helping customers succeed. If we sound like your kind of people, join us!

About The Role

We are seeking a Senior Competitive & Market Intelligence Manager to build and lead the intelligence capability that helps us understand where the market is going, how competitors are evolving, where WEKA has the right to win, and what we need to do about it.

This is a technical, hands-on builder role. You will design and scale the systems, tools, operating rhythms, and feedback loops that turn fragmented competitive, customer, field, and market signals into a trusted intelligence engine for the company. You'll go deep on competitors and market dynamics, develop clear points of view, and translate what you learn into positioning, competitive deal strategies, field tools, technical briefs, training decks, product insights, and recommendations that help WEKA stay ahead in a fast-moving AI infrastructure market.

Reporting to the VP of Product Marketing, you'll work closely with Product, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Marketing, Alliances, GTM Operations, and executive leadership. You'll serve as a trusted source of intelligence across the company, helping teams understand not simply what is changing, but what it means for WEKA and what we should do next.

Who We’re Looking For

You're a senior builder. You've created or materially scaled a competitive or market intelligence capability before, and you understand everything required to make it work: sources, tools, processes, field feedback loops, operating cadence, executive communication, enablement, and measurement. You're comfortable starting with a blank page, deciding what matters, and building a system people actually trust and use.

You're intellectually curious, analytical, and technical enough to go well beyond competitor websites and marketing claims. You can dig into products, architectures, benchmarks, customer experiences, business models, and go-to-market strategies, separate signal from noise, and develop a defensible point of view about where competitors are strong, where they're vulnerable, and where the market is headed.

You also know intelligence only matters if it changes decisions and outcomes. You can turn deep research into a concise executive recommendation, a sharp competitive position, or a field tool a seller can use in a live deal. You stay close to Sales, Product, customers, and the market, and measure success by better decisions and stronger competitive performance, not the volume of research produced.

What You’ll Be Working On

Build the Intelligence Engine: Design and scale WEKA's competitive and market intelligence program, including sources, tooling, workflows, taxonomy, operating cadence, governance, distribution, and feedback loops. Create a trusted system of record that stays current as the market evolves.
Own Competitive Intelligence: Develop deep intelligence on priority competitors across products, architecture, performance, positioning, customers, partnerships, business models, and go-to-market strategy. Identify strengths, vulnerabilities, strategic moves, and likely next steps.
Monitor Competitive Pricing & Packaging: Track competitor pricing, packaging, licensing, consumption models, and commercial changes, and surface meaningful shifts to Product and other stakeholders to inform pricing and packaging decisions.
Drive Market Intelligence: Track the forces reshaping AI infrastructure, including technology shifts, market structure, customer requirements, emerging categories and competitors, cloud and neocloud dynamics, ecosystem moves, business models, and buying patterns. Translate those signals into implications and opportunities for WEKA.
Turn Intelligence Into Strategy: Synthesize competitive, market, customer, and field signals into clear points of view and actionable recommendations that inform company positioning, product strategy, go-to-market priorities, category strategy, and where WEKA should invest, defend, or differentiate.
Create Competitive Positioning & Tools: Develop and continuously improve competitive positioning, battlecards, playbooks, objection handling, comparison frameworks, executive briefs, and other tools that help Sales, Solutions Engineering, partners, and Marketing differentiate WEKA and win.
Build the Field Intelligence Loop: Establish scalable ways to capture what sellers, SEs, partners, prospects, and customers are seeing in the market. Partner with Sales and GTM Operations to turn competitive deal data, field feedback, and win/loss insights into intelligence that improves positioning, enablement, and strategy.
Support Competitive Deals: Engage directly with Sales and Solutions Engineering on strategic competitive opportunities, helping teams understand the competitor, sharpen the strategy, respond to claims, and apply what is learned back into the broader intelligence program.
Deliver Executive Intelligence: Establish a consistent cadence of concise, decision-oriented competitive and market briefings for Product, GTM, and executive leadership, surfacing meaningful changes, emerging threats and opportunities, and recommended actions.
Apply AI & Automation: Use AI, automation, and modern intelligence tools to continuously monitor market signals, accelerate research and synthesis, and deliver intelligence in the workflows where teams need it. Apply strong judgment to ensure automation increases signal rather than noise.
Influence Product & Marketing: Partner closely with Product and Product Marketing to bring competitive and market insights into roadmap discussions, positioning and messaging, launches, category strategy, campaigns, and thought leadership.
Leverage Analyst & Industry Insights: Work with Analyst Relations and other external intelligence sources to incorporate analyst research, industry perspectives, market data, and third-party validation into WEKA's view of the market and competitive landscape.
Measure Impact: Establish practical measures of success including intelligence adoption, field engagement, competitive win/loss trends, effectiveness of competitive plays, and demonstrated influence on product, positioning, and GTM decisions.

Qualifications

6+ years of experience in competitive intelligence, market intelligence, product marketing, product strategy, management consulting, industry research, or a closely related role in enterprise technology.
Demonstrated experience personally building or materially scaling a competitive or market intelligence program, including the systems, tools, processes, operating cadence, and feedback loops required to make it sustainable. We are looking for someone who has built the muscle, not simply participated in an established program.
Strong experience conducting competitive research and analysis and translating complex findings into clear positioning, recommendations, enablement, and executive-level insights.
Strong technical aptitude and the ability to independently understand enterprise infrastructure architectures, product capabilities, performance claims, integrations, and technical differentiation.
Working knowledge of AI/ML infrastructure, accelerated computing, cloud computing, data platforms, storage and memory technologies, or adjacent enterprise infrastructure technologies.
Experience building field intelligence and win/loss programs, working directly with Sales, Solutions Engineering, customers, and GTM Operations to understand real-world competitive dynamics.
Strong primary and secondary research skills with the ability to synthesize product research, customer and field feedback, analyst research, market data, public information, and other signals into a clear point of view.
Exceptional written, visual, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to move from deep analysis to concise battlecards, executive briefings, presentations, and strategic recommendations.
Experience using AI, automation, and competitive or market intelligence tools to improve the speed, scale, and quality of intelligence programs.
Proven ability to influence Product, Sales, Marketing, and executive stakeholders without direct authority and turn intelligence into action.
Strong business judgment and an outcome-oriented mindset, with the ability to prioritize the competitors, market questions, and intelligence work most likely to influence customers, strategy, pipeline, and revenue.
Comfortable operating as a senior individual contributor in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with significant autonomy and evolving priorities.
Bachelor's degree in a relevant technical or business field, or equivalent practical experience.
Located in North America with the ability to travel up to 25%.

How We Work: The WEKA Way

We are Accountable: We take full ownership, always, even when things don't go as planned. We lead with integrity, show up with responsibility and ownership, and hold ourselves and each other to the highest standards.
We are Brave: We question the status quo, push boundaries, and take smart risks when needed. We welcome challenges and embrace debates as opportunities for growth, turning courage into fuel for innovation.
We are Collaborative: True collaboration isn't only about working together. It's about lifting one another up to succeed collectively. We are team-oriented and communicate with empathy and respect. We challenge each other, resolve conflict constructively, and are transparent about our goals and the results we achieve. Together, we're unstoppable.
We are Customer Centric: Our customers are at the heart of everything we do. We actively listen and prioritize their success, and every decision we make is driven by how we can better serve, support, and empower them to succeed. When our customers win, we win.

Concerned you don’t meet every qualification? Don’t let it stop you from applying!

Studies have shown that traditionally underrepresented groups may be less likely to apply for jobs if they don’t meet every qualification specified. WEKA is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. If you are excited about this position but are concerned your past work experience doesn’t match up perfectly with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles at WEKA.

jobs.title: Engineering Program Manager, Devices
jobs.description:
About Atomic Machines:

Atomic Machines is ushering in a new era of micromanufacturing with its Matter Compiler™ technology platform. This platform enables new classes of micromachines to be designed and built by providing manufacturing processes and a materials library that are inaccessible to semiconductor manufacturing methods. It unlocks MEMS manufacturing not only for device classes that could never be produced by semiconductor methods, but also for entirely new categories. Furthermore, this digital platform is fully programmable in the way 3D printing is digital, but whereas 3D printing produces parts of a single material using a single process, the Matter Compiler™ technology platform is a multi-process, multi-material system: bits and raw materials go in, and complete, functional micromachines come out. The Atomic Machines team has also created an exciting first device, made possible only through the Matter Compiler™ technology platform, addressing a critical need in the rapidly evolving AI data center world, and we are commercializing it now.

Our offices are in Emeryville and Santa Clara, California.

About The Role:

We are seeking a highly technical Engineering Program Manager to own the program for that first device's successor, end to end: from requirements still maturing with lead customers, through qualification, certification, and manufacturing scale-up on the Matter Compiler, to commercial launch. That successor is a new class of micromachine, made possible only by the Matter Compiler, and you will be the leader that delivers it.

At Atomic Machines, Program Management is a leverage function, and its core skill is clarity. The Device program's technical leadership is already in place: device design, process, test, and reliability are each led by deep domain owners who move fast and expect the same. You lead that team as one program, and you drive the outcome, integrated plan, customer commitments, tradeoffs, operating cadence, and decisions that keep every discipline moving as one. Technical direction belongs to the domain owners; turning their work into the outcomes of certified, scaling, revenue-generating products belongs to you. This role is for someone who was an individual contributor in complex technical domains and moved into program leadership on purpose: to influence product direction, align engineering and manufacturing, and own outcomes end to end.

What You'll Do:

Develop and drive the program roadmap end to end: set goals, define milestones and evidence gates, and build the accountability structure that connects daily engineering work to business outcomes and customer commitments.
Direct cross-functional execution across device physics, fabrication processes, automation, and system integration: set the deliverables, sequencing, and resource calls for engineering, operations, and leadership.
Build and run the integrated plan connecting customer commitments, design maturity, process capability, and manufacturing readiness. Run the operating cadence that keeps it honest.
Turn maturing customer requirements into committed, testable targets, and hold the program to them.
Build the program structures that keep device and process development in lockstep with the Matter Compiler platform. Move development from R&D into production and define what each handoff must prove.
Structure the program around evidence and short learning loops: design the build-test-learn iteration cycles, give every open unknown an experiment with a pass/fail criterion, and let the schedule follow from results.
Own the qualification and certification path (e.g., UL/IEC) as a program commitment shaped into the design from day one.
Deliver the outcome: the device demonstrated, evaluated by lead customers, and qualified through production ramp.
Institutionalize what you learn: build the systems, rhythms, and decision structures the whole organization runs on, so the next program moves faster than this one.

What You'll Need:

8+ years spanning hands-on engineering and technical program leadership on complex multidisciplinary hardware: you have personally taken things from thought to build and owned programs that others depended on.
A track record of taking integrated hardware systems from concept through manufacturing release and commercial delivery, with the judgment to know when a decision needs more rigor and when to move fast.
Deep technical fluency in at least one core engineering domain and productive command across the rest: you hold your own with engineers designing in coupled physical domains — electromagnetics, structural mechanics, thermal behavior, fluidics, and materials.
You drive senior technical leads to deliver at a high level: clarity, structure, and pace, while technical direction stays with the domain owner.
Relentlessness in driving through ambiguity: turning unresolved requirements into scope, evidence gates, and a plan the team runs.
Conviction in iterative hardware development and short learning loops — build early, test early, learn fast, continually finding the shortest learning loop.
True Ownership of your program and domain, with bottom-line-up-front communication, trusted by engineers and leadership alike. The strongest people you've worked with would choose to work with you again.
BS or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Materials Science.

Nice to Have:

Reliability engineering for microscale or precision devices: accelerated life testing, environmental stress testing, and long-term performance characterization.
Experience driving a product through UL, IEC, or equivalent certification.
Experience standing up programs from ground zero, then driving reliability growth to manufacturing scale.

jobs.description:
Description

Enphase Energy is a global energy technology company and a leading provider of solar, battery, and electric vehicle charging products. Founded in 2006, our innovative microinverter technology revolutionized solar power, making it a safer, more reliable, and scalable energy source. Today, the Enphase Energy System enables users to make, use, save, and sell their own power. Enphase is also one of the most successful and innovative clean energy companies in the world, with more than 80 million products shipped across 160 countries.

Enphase is now extending its proven distributed power architecture beyond residential and commercial solar into large-scale infrastructure with the IQ Solid-State Transformer (IQ SST) — a GaN-based, semiconductor- and software-defined power platform purpose-built for AI and hyperscale data centers. Each IQ SST rack combines intelligent power modules operating in a coordinated series/parallel configuration to convert medium-voltage grid power directly to usable AC and DC voltages for data centers including AI and machine learning applications, and the platform is designed to scale to gigawatt-level deployments. Join us in bringing this next-generation product from advanced development through engineering validation and into production.

The Role

The Senior Project Manager, IQ SST is responsible for planning and driving the internal engineering and New Product Introduction (NPI) projects that make up the IQ SST development program. Working out of our Austin, Texas facility, you will guide projects through Enphase's product realization process in a highly cross-functional environment — developing and maintaining project schedules, partnering with procurement, tracking vendor deliveries, and keeping engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams aligned and informed. You will own the operating rhythm of the projects you manage: running team meetings, tracking actions and risks, and communicating progress clearly so each project moves through its development and validation gates on time, at quality, and at cost.

What You Will Do

Plan and drive internal engineering and NPI projects across the IQ SST platform, guiding them through each phase of Enphase's product realization process from concept through validation and production readiness.
Develop, baseline, and maintain detailed, integrated project schedules covering design milestones, prototype builds, component qualification, test and validation phases, and phase-gate reviews.
Partner closely with Procurement on sourcing plans and purchase order execution; track vendor and supplier deliveries against the schedule and drive resolution when materials or components are at risk.
Coordinate cross-functional execution across Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing/Operations, Quality, and Compliance, ensuring dependencies are visible and owned.
Support engineering build planning and execution, including material readiness, build coordination, and post-build issue tracking and disposition.
Identify, track, and drive resolution of project risks and blockers — design changes, part shortages, test failures, tooling delays, and compliance holds — before they impact schedule.
Run core team meetings, design reviews, and phase-gate reviews; capture decisions and action items and drive follow-through.
Provide crisp project status, dashboards, and executive-level updates, clearly communicating progress, trade-offs, risks, and recovery plans to teams and senior stakeholders.
Partner with the IQ SST program management team to roll project-level plans into the overall program schedule, and help develop and improve project management processes as the team scales.
Champion project management process improvements and tooling, including productive uses of AI and automation to reduce overhead on the team.

What You Bring

8+ years of experience as a Senior Project Manager driving complex, high-value projects in renewable energy, energy storage, power electronics, or related technology and infrastructure sectors.
Expertise in project planning, baseline schedule development and management, resource allocation, risk mitigation, and stakeholder engagement across internal teams and external vendors.
Experience working with procurement and managing suppliers and vendors through execution — tracking commitments and deliveries, holding partners accountable to schedule and quality, and reporting performance.
Demonstrated success operating in highly cross-functional environments, coordinating engineering, procurement, manufacturing, and quality teams toward common milestones.
Proven track record delivering projects safely, on time, and within budget, with disciplined performance reporting and variance management.
Proficiency with industry-standard project management tools such as Primavera P6 and Microsoft Project, and strong command of dashboards and status reporting.
Exceptional communication skills — written, verbal, and via dashboards/status reporting — with the ability to drive clarity and alignment across technical and business stakeholders, up to and including executives.
Demonstrated ability to lead high-velocity projects with significant internal and external dependencies and to drive decisions in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related technical field; MBA or advanced degree a plus. PMP certification or equivalent a plus.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with structured product development or product realization processes, including phase-gate reviews and NPI, or a strong desire to apply large-project delivery discipline to new product development.
Background in utility-scale solar, BESS, or data center electrical equipment — helpful context for the markets IQ SST serves.
Experience launching a new product or technology platform into a new market segment.
Experience with domestic/US manufacturing scale-up and related sourcing considerations.
Experience using automation, scripting, or dashboards to manage project data at scale.

It's a new day with a new opportunity at 8am!

About the role:

As we evolve our security posture to meet growth and regulatory expectations, we are seeking a transformational Senior Information Security Manager to lead our technical security team and operationalize security capabilities that are measurable, effective, and aligned with business priorities. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will lead the day-to-day execution of the security program and directly manage the security engineering and analyst team, while partnering closely with the U.S.-based VP of Information Security and the compliance and privacy operations team.

Location: Czech Republic (Remote). Working hours for this role are aligned to U.S. Central Time (Austin) core business hours to ensure real-time collaboration with the U.S.-based security leadership and compliance team.

This role is hired through an Employer of Record (EOR) partner in the Czech Republic.

About us:

8am builds software that helps professionals run stronger businesses. Our platform powers payments, client experience, and operational workflows for legal, accounting, and other service-based businesses. U.S. based professionals count on our purpose-built solutions to simplify operations, ensure compliance, and fuel profitable growth, so they can focus on their clients and do more of the work that matters.

More than 250,000 professionals across the U.S. rely on our products every day. As we continue to grow, we're investing in the next generation of our platform and are looking for experienced engineers who want to help shape its future.

What you'll do:

Team leadership
: Lead and develop the security engineering/analyst team — delivery, prioritization, coaching, performance
Security operations
: Own security platforms (EDR, SIEM, compliance automation, vulnerability management, CSPM) and detection/response workflows
Metrics & reporting
: Own security metrics pipeline (remediation velocity, control assurance, coverage) for quarterly business reviews
AI security
: Drive AI adoption in tooling for better detection, and define/enforce security standards for AI/agentic systems (LLM integrations, orchestration, governance)
Incident & compliance leadership
: Lead incident response (EU hours, US coordination), post-incident reviews, and partner on compliance audits (SOC 2, PCI DSS, EU regs)
Security design reviews
: Lead design reviews across product lines with risk ratings, SLAs, and documented standards
Threat intel & detection engineering
: Monitor relevant threat intel and convert into actionable detections
Fraud/attack investigation
: Partner cross-functionally to investigate attacks (card testing, fraud, abuse), turning findings into detections and hardening recommendations

About you:

7+ years in information security, including 2+ years leading technical security staff.
Hands-on depth in cloud security operations (AWS preferred), SIEM/log analytics, EDR platforms, and vulnerability management programs.
Track record of building measurable, metrics-driven security programs in a compliance-heavy environment (PCI DSS, SOC 2, or equivalent).
Experience operating in distributed, cross-timezone teams; excellent written communication.
Fluent professional English.
Demonstrated experience leveraging AI tools and technologies to improve workflows, enhance decision-making, or drive innovation.
This position is preferably based in Brno, Czech Republic

Bonus points:

Experience securing or governing AI/LLM systems and agentic tooling.
Familiarity with EU regulatory landscape (GDPR) and fintech or legal-tech domains.

Additional Information

The monthly gross salary range for this position is CZK 95,000 to CZK 175,000. 8am is committed to fair, objective, and non-discriminatory compensation, and actual pay may vary based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and education.

Why join our new 8am Brno hub?

Founding Team Impact:
Be a founding engineer of our new Brno R&D hub. After a brief 1-6 month integration with U.S. based teams, you will help form fully autonomous, locally-led squads with clear paths to Staff and leadership roles
Drive our "AI-First" Transformation:
We are building a secure, massive-scale "Unified AI Platform". Depending on your squad, you will either help architect this core infrastructure (LLM routing, RAG, agent orchestration) or build directly on top of it.
Build the Next Generation of Our Platform:
Help shape the systems powering products used by more than 250,000 professionals. You'll work on complex platform capabilities across payments, workflow automation, and AI-powered features as we expand into new professional service markets.

Benefits and Perks

We offer a competitive, locally relevant benefits package designed to support your life in the Czech Republic while giving you access to global opportunities:

Performance bonus opportunities
and employee referral rewards
Flexible Time Off (FTO)
and 13 paid public holidays aligned with the Czech calendar
Paid sick leave
with additional support through the Czech social security system
Maternity, paternity, and parental leave
in line with Czech regulations, plus additional paid paternity leave from 8am
Full statutory benefits
, including public health insurance, social security, pension, and work accident coverage

Grow Your Career

Access to Coursera (including Gen AI Academy) and ongoing professional development
Clear growth paths, regular feedback, and opportunities for advancement

International company environment
with collaboration across Europe and the U.S.
Opportunities to travel for company events (including potential U.S. visits)
Engaging team culture with local events, outings, and community initiatives
High-quality company swag and programs focused on wellness, learning, and connection

At 8am, we recognize that innovation occurs with a strong team of people who are diverse in background, personality, talent and ideas. Experience comes in many forms and ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace where we continue to learn from each other is an integral part of our culture. We are committed to creating a welcoming and transparent environment for all that embraces those differences through education, equal access to opportunities and information, inclusionary programs, and community outreach.

The Sr. Project Manager has primary responsibility for the management of medium to large scale projects which often require larger project teams and/or cross functional teams or multiple non-related projects. The Sr. Project Manager will manage projects from original concept through final implementation/warranty, managing stakeholder involvement, customer satisfaction and customer impact throughout, using established governance standards and processes. The Sr. Project Manager will lead the project team to proactively identify risks and issues that could challenge project delivery and will ensure those risks and issues are mitigated or resolved. The Sr. Project Manager will establish the appropriate governance in line with Markel standards and track benefits throughout the project lifecycle. 

In this role, the Sr. Project Manager has the overall responsibility and accountability to drive projects to success as defined by the project sponsors and key stakeholders. This role will work with internal and external customers, third party vendors, governance, and senior management in accomplishing project objectives.

Facilitate the execution of medium to large scale projects by providing strategic direction to project team, fostering effective working relationships between team members, and taking appropriate action to optimize team performance.

Identify, assess, and manage risk to the success of the project.
Effectively create and deliver presentations to project team and key stakeholders, communicating project status.
Leverage problem solving and influencing skills to ensure that project deliverables are completed within agreed cost and timeline and are approved by key stakeholders and sponsors. Collaborate with change management team on change management plans including communications, training, etc.

We’re all about people | We win together | We strive for better

In keeping with the values of the Markel Style, we strive to support our employees in living their lives to the fullest at home and at work.

jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About The Role

Business Operations is Rippling’s strike team for high-stakes, mission-critical challenges. We are the architects behind product development, go-to-market strategies, and scale operations across the entire company. Operating as the connective tissue for our compound startup, this small, elite unit brings structure to massive ambiguity and executes with relentless precision.

We need BizOps Managers who are world-class problem solvers, first-principles thinkers, and fearless operators. You won't just advise, you will build from 0-to-1, tackle the company’s biggest strategic bets, and partner directly with executive leadership. For high-performers, this role is the ultimate launchpad into executive leadership at an ultra-high-growth company.

What You'll Do

Hunt Down High-Impact Problems: Identify critical business friction points, step into the fire, and build scalable solutions alongside senior leaders.
Master the Revenue Engine: Architect and refine monetization, pricing, and packaging strategies to aggressively accelerate market dominance.
Drive Cross-Functional Force-Multiplier Projects: Partner directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams to launch new initiatives and revolutionize operational systems.
Own Your Data: Dig into raw databases, build custom SQL queries, construct dashboards, and extract actionable insight without needing a safety net.
Set the Source of Truth: Collaborate with Finance and RevOps to define, standardize, and scale the operational metrics that steer the entire business.

What You'll Need

4+ years of battle-tested experience in top-tier management consulting, BizOps, VC/PE, or as a startup founder. Exceptional talent with fewer years but a proven track record of rapid acceleration will be considered.
Cross-functional mastery: A deep understanding of organizational dynamics in high-velocity tech environments.
A data-first instinct: You instinctively open a spreadsheet, code a query, or analyze a dataset before building a slide deck.
Extreme altitude-switching: Equally comfortable pitching strategy to C-suite executives as you are getting into the weeds with frontline operators.
Relentless ownership and grit: You don't pass the mic or make excuses—you take full accountability and solve problems permanently.
High-conviction autonomy: You thrive in chaos, make sound calls with incomplete data, and move fast without waiting for a playbook.

Rippling is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Senior Staff Deployment Strategist, Operations
jobs.description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.

ALSO is becoming a manufacturer, with serialized vehicles moving from production lines to customers. The systems to manage that transition largely don’t exist yet.

You’ll build ALSO’s operating system for making and moving vehicles—from CM production to the customer’s door—creating a single source of truth for planning, quality, inventory, delivery, and decision-making. Today, much of this runs on spreadsheets and tribal knowledge; you’ll turn it into scalable systems and close the loop so decisions happen within them.

As the Senior Staff Deployment Strategist, Operations,
you’ll help take ALSO from startup to a mature, class-leading operator. You’ll report to our Director of Enterprise Data and work closely with supply chain, manufacturing, quality, finance, and commercial teams. There are no direct reports today; you’ll lead through architecture, code, and influence.

What You Will Do

Build end-to-end visibility from factory to customer: WIP, first-pass yield, as-built genealogy from module to vehicle, inventory down to supplier-held stock, and shipment status.
Build the planning engine across both supply chains, what we buy from our CMs and what we assemble ourselves: material planning at SKU-by-day, available-to-promise, and the build and fulfillment queues.
Run the supplier loop: PO confirmations, promise dates, RFQs, design changes, the forecast we release to tiers 1 through 3, and component pricing with effectivity.
Run the physical moves: booking, importation and track-and-trace from CM to 3PL to customer, plus the visibility feed out of our CMs’ own systems.
Close the quality loop: incoming and inline quality, deviations and trends, warranty tracing, and a defect traced to a supplier chargeback that lands in the financial system.
Settle buy-versus-build by shipping: stand up a thin, disposable app for quality, transport and warehouse visibility, run the process instrumented, and let evidence pick the platform we buy later.
Engineer the process before you automate it: instrument how the work actually runs, including the exceptions nobody wrote down, delete the steps that exist only because two systems could not talk, then automate what survives. Paving the cowpath faster is not the job.
Ship with coding agents in days rather than quarters.
Embed with the team that owns a process, automate it with them, and leave them able to change it themselves. Success is the owner shipping their own improvements, not filing tickets for you.

What You Will Bring

8+ years building operations, manufacturing or supply chain software from zero to production, owning the data model and decision logic. Technical degree or equivalent hands-on experience.
Daily LLM-native development with coding agents such as Claude, and a real method for proving model output correct: contracts, tests, evals and review.
A track record of rapid iteration: working software in users’ hands in days, then improved from how it actually gets used.
Deep SaaS platform expertise: integrating QMS, TMS, WMS or ERP into one data platform, and the judgment to know when a package earns its place and when it is the slow path.
Python, SQL and API fluency, plus enough physical-operations sense to turn conflicting data into one honest picture.
Comfort earning an unfamiliar team's trust, and moving to the next constraint once the automation is live.
Willingness to travel internationally to our contract manufacturers in Taiwan when the work calls for it.

This role includes regular on-site presence in Palo Alto, time on the warehouse floor, and occasional international travel. The salary for this position ranges from $170,000 to $225,000 per year,
depending on experience and qualifications.

Perks And Benefits

Robust health coverage. Excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by ALSO with FSA & HSA options.
One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates.
Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny.
Flexible time off.
401(k) match.

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces.

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

Overview

Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc. (SPA) delivers high-impact, technical solutions to complex national security issues. With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. Our exceptionally talented team is highly collaborative in spirit and practice, producing Results that Matter . Come work with the best! We offer opportunity, unique challenges, and clear-sighted commitment to the mission. SPA: Objective. Responsive. Trusted.

The Space and Intelligence Division provides professional services to the US Space Force, Combatant Commands, Intelligence Community, and NASA. Our work includes enterprise architectural assessments, systems engineering and integration, test, planning and execution, cost estimating and analysis, acquisition support, and cybersecurity. We are trusted partners developing approaches and concepts to meet emerging high priority needs, assessing cutting-edge technologies, and supporting capabilities for our National Defense. Come join the fastest growing Division at Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc.

The Strategic Technology Analysis Group, part of SPA’s Space and Intelligence Division, offers sophisticated capabilities (people, process & tools) to resolve unique problems in space, cyber, and special operations in support to military services, Secretary of Defense offices (OSD) and theater warfighters. Our portfolio includes the Assistant Secretary of Air Force for Space Acquisition & Integration (SAF/SQ), Joint Warfare Analysis Center (JWAC), Space Security and Defense Program (SSDP), National Space Defense Center (NSDC), Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC), Strategic Capabilities Office (SCO), US Space Command (USSPACECOM) and US Space Force (USSF). Collaborate and integrate across diverse teams to achieve insightful analytic findings that aid decision makers.

10+ years of leading and integrating DoW and IC system engineering, operations research, and/or cross-domain studies and analysis
